title_original: Joe Russo teases final ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ trailer: “Keep refreshing your feed”
excerpt_original: “I can make an argument that everyone should just go and see the movie now,” says Russo.

blocks.text: Joe Russo has teased that a final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday could yet be released in the four weeks before the film comes out.
Russo, co-director on the film with his brother Anthony Russo, was speaking at the Doha Industry Days at Qatar’s Doha Film Festival, organised by the Film Committee at Media City Qatar.

“My guess is some time between now and the movie coming out [on December 18 through Disney], you should keep checking, keep refreshing your feed,” said Russo, in response to a question about whether a final trailer for the film was imminent. The Russo brothers produce the film through their company AGBO.

Trailers and teasers for the film have been released across the last 11 months, starting with a short teaser before screenings of Disney stablemate Avatar: Fire And Ash last December, confirming the return of Steve Rogers (Chris Evans). Further teasers were then released confirming that Thor (Chris Hemsworth), the X-Men, the Wakandans and the Fantastic Four would all feature in the film.
The first full trailer launched at CinemaCon in April 2026, before releasing online on July 20. A special look then followed online on August 15.

“I have to interact with the fans to understand what is moving them, what is working for them,” said Russo in Doha. “What we’ve been doing with Doomsday is very different than the last time we did this, because the speed of conversation on the internet is even faster than it was in 2018, 2019.

“I had this idea of: why don’t we start the story a year earlier,” said Russo. “Why don’t we start dropping clues in the year leading up to the movie? We did four trailers that were sprinkled out. The story started in January of last year, and you’ve been watching it slowly unfold. These are all pieces of something that are going to equal two-and-a-half hours of your time on December 18. But it’s slowly investing emotionally.

“I’m also getting feedback as that’s happening, and we can make adjustments as we go based on what people are tracking on not tracking. I have a very complicated story bill, so I have to make sure that they’re following each little problem we give them. If they get the wrong thing from it, then I have to make adjustments, knowing coming in that they might have the wrong idea.”

“Every time we post something that’s not a trailer, our comments are filled with hate for the fact that it was not a trailer,” smiled Russo. “I can tell when [the fans] are getting anxious for more material. There’s been plenty of material out there. I can make an argument that everybody should just go see the movie now. Somebody will still hunt me down for that.”

Russo spoke warmly about the passionate Avengers fanbase, in contrast to “the spigot of noise” that is found elsewhere on the internet. “There’s no question that there are a lot of people with unhealthy tendencies that exist with a megaphone on the internet. Lots people make the argument that that’s all that exists. But there are true fans out there, people who really care. They’re passionate and want to participate, to immerse, to be part of the conversation. They want to talk to other people who are just as passionate as they are. Those are the people we’re interested in.”
Just four weeks out from the Doomsday release, Russo expressed his disbelief that “two guys from Cleveland on borrowed time” [he and his brother] were in this position.

“We didn’t have these kinds of dreams,” said the filmmaker. “It’s hard to process sometimes, because I think I’m a kid sitting in the front row watching The Empire Strikes Back at 10 years old, and being so fascinated and moved by it. I did it three or four times in one day. I’m just trying to replicate that same feeling I had for other kids elsewhere.”
Doha Industry Days conclude tomorrow, with Doha Film Festival running until Friday, November 27.
